# bank-java

> Java 21+ and Kotlin library that reads a Czech bank's payment notification e-mail into a `Transaction`, and hands
> it out only once the bank's DKIM signature verified, with the bank's key validated through DNSSEC and pinned in the
> release. Air Bank and Fio banka in Czechia so far. One artifact, `cz.insuit:bank-notifications`, no framework required. Published on
> GitHub Packages (group `cz.insuit`), not Maven Central. Pre-1.0: read records by accessor, never by record pattern.

Setting it up in a project:

- Add `cz.insuit:bank-notifications`; DKIM verification is inside it, there is nothing else to add or configure.
- Add the GitHub Packages repository `https://maven.pkg.github.com/landsman/bank-java`. It asks for a token even for
  a public package (`read:packages`). Never write a token into the build file or the repository.
- One `BankNotifications.withDns()` per application, it is thread-safe. `read(rawMessage)` returns a `Transaction`
  or throws a sealed `BankNotificationException`: `Unverified`, `TemporaryFailure` or `Unparsed`.
- The account holder switches the bank's e-mail on and sends it straight to an address the application receives.

Mistakes to avoid:

- Hand `read` the message bytes exactly as they arrived, headers included. A message re-serialised by a mail library
  no longer matches its signature and is `Unverified` every time.
- Store the raw bytes before reading them: `Unparsed` and `TemporaryFailure` can be read again later.
- Branch on `Unparsed.reason()`, never on the message text: `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` is the one to show the account holder,
  with `getMessage()` saying what to change in their banking.
- Never act on `Unverified`: anyone can send an e-mail that looks like the bank's.
- A valid signature does not prove the e-mail is about your account: compare `account()` with the one you expect.
- Use `readAll()` where one e-mail may report several transactions (ČSOB); `read()` refuses such an e-mail.
- Deduplicate on `transactionId()`, per bank: the same e-mail can arrive twice. `messageId()` is set only when the
  bank signs it; never deduplicate on a `Message-ID` header read elsewhere, which a copy of the e-mail can change.
- `balance()` is the balance right after the payment and may be `null`; never take it for the account's current balance.
- `counterAccount()` is `null` for a card payment; `account()` and `transactionId()` are `null` for MONETA, which
  masks the account and prints no id: tell the merchant by the inbound address, deduplicate on a signed `messageId()`.
- `amount()` is signed: negative is money out. `Transaction.Type` may gain constants: keep a `default` branch.
- Messages over 64 KiB are `Unparsed`; a notification is around 5 KiB.
- Do not use `trustingKeysFrom` in production: it skips DNSSEC and pinning. It is for tests.
- Do not return a `Transaction` from a controller as JSON: it carries the payer's name, account and message.
- `message()` and `counterName()` are untrusted text the payer typed, handed out unescaped: bind them as SQL
  parameters and let templates escape them; never concatenate them into a query, HTML or a command.

## Docs

- [Installing](https://github.com/landsman/bank-java/blob/main/.docs/install.md): the repository block and the token, for Gradle and Maven
- [Setting up a bank](https://github.com/landsman/bank-java/blob/main/.docs/setup.md): how the account holder points the bank's e-mail at your address
- [Using the library](https://github.com/landsman/bank-java/blob/main/.docs/usage.md): the raw message, the exceptions, a transaction's fields, the two checks left to you
- [How verification works](https://github.com/landsman/bank-java/blob/main/.docs/verification.md): what makes a signature count, DNSSEC, pinning, the size limit
